# Poisson Binomial Distribution

## Overview

The Poisson Binomial distribution is somewhat similar to the Beta Binomial distribution. Instead of sampling the probability from a distribution, we know the probability of each outcome.

## Description

This distribution generalizes the binomial distribution by allowing each Bernoulli trial to have a different probability of success. In the standard binomial distribution, all trials have the same probability $p$, but in the Poisson Binomial, each trial $i$ has its own probability $p_i$.

## Probability Density Function

$$Pr(K = k) = \sum_{A \in F_k} \prod_{i \in A} p_i \prod_{j \in A^c} (1-p_j)$$

Where:
- $F_k$ = all combinations of k integers that can be selected from 1:n
- Example: $F_2$ with n = 1,2,3 = {{1,2}, {1,3}, {2,3}}
- $A$ = the set of a particular combination, e.g., {1,2} in the above example
- $A^c$ = the complementary set of A, e.g., if A = {{1,2}}, then A^c = {{1,3},{2,3}}

## Interpretation

Generally speaking, this means that the probability of a particular k (number of successes) is the sum of the product of probabilities of all possible combinations that result in k successes.

## Real-world Examples

- Sports: probability of winning k games when each game has a different probability
- Finance: probability of k investments being profitable with different success probabilities
- Medicine: probability of k patients responding to treatment with different response rates
